He mentions a narration on the authority of Abdah who states that the messenger of Allah sallallam said the people of paradise they will eat in paradise and they will drink in paradise. However, they will not relieve themselves. They will not use the bathroom. They will not have to blow their noses. They will not have to urinate or evacuate their bowels. Ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra ra rather that food that they eat will turn into a kind of energy that they will embody and will then resonate from their bodies and will have the distinct smell of musk. So here we see in this narration that the people of paradise are overwhelmed with thankfulness to Allah subhanahu wa'ta'ala. They are so overwhelmed that with every breath they make and of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala and that's really what got them there in the first place. Right? And so that is part of their paradise. Part of their paradise is the remembrance of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. That's what gives them inner pleasure just as paradise gives them outer and physical pleasure. Also we see again the word musk. Musk comes up a lot in the Quran and the Sunnah with respect to paradise. For instance, Allah mentions musk very often u or or in multiple places in the Quran with respect to the fragrance of paradise. In Sah Muslim anis narrates that the prophet sallall.aii alaihi wasallam describes Alar which is the river that is al that Allah gave to him and he describes this river as its banks being of pure musk. Usually a banks of a river is mud right mud and dirt. But nothing is disposable in paradise. Everything is of quality and of consequence. And so the banks of that river are musk. Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala tells us that the drinks the sealed nectar wine that very dense and very potent wine of paradise will be sealed with seals of musk. Meaning the wax seals will be of musk and also it will have notes of musk when a person drinks it. Now what is musk? I mean a lot of us have heard of it. probably not many of us if any of us have ever really seen musk. Real musk. Musk is something that is harvested from a very specific deer in Asia. It's a very bizarre, creepy looking deer. It's a deer that has fangs a dog, a mountain lion. It has no antlers. It has fangs coming out of its mouth a mountain lion. And this deer, every year around mating season, it has a musk gland that produces this musk and they use it for mating and marking territory. Now this gland is harvested but these deer are very elusive. They are very fast and they are lone. They don't go around in herds. They they are very isolate creatures kind of wolves. So they're hard to hunt. And when a deer is you know hunted and when it is captured and and and butchered, they harvest the musk gland. And it has to be harvested at a very specific time of the year. And this musk gland, when all the musk is taken out of it, it is a very thick resin. And it smells very strong, not good. It's not a pleasant smell when it's first harvested, but then they dry it. And sometimes they smoke it. And sometimes they have other techniques and as it dries out, it becomes little rocks or grains of sand. And it's actually brown and red. Looks just like dark rich dirt. And this musk then has a very nice smell. This is imported from Asia during the prophet sallall.aii wasallam's time and it still is because you can only harvest it from that one deer. And so the highest levels of royalty in Arabian culture during the time of the prophet sallall.aii wasallam was that of musk. This was extremely expensive, very rarely found and usually only used by royalty in the highest of settings and the most premier of drinks and foods and so forth. And so when Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala mentions musk in the Quran, yes, there is musk, but it's also more than that, right? It also mentions that the highest of premiere, the highest, the most elite of scents and tastes and colors are what awaits people of paradise and you shall fear Muhammad. >>.

summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the descriptions of paradise from Sahih Muslim, focusing on a hadith from Abdullah that details the unique characteristics of life in paradise. He explains that the people of paradise will eat and drink, but their bodies will not require elimination; instead, their food will be transformed into energy that produces the fragrance of musk. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that the inhabitants of paradise will be constantly engaged in remembrance of Allah (subhan'Allah and Alhamdulillah) with every breath they take, illustrating how thankfulness is integral to their eternal reward. He also explores the significance of musk in paradise, noting its repeated mention in both the Quran and Sunnah—from the banks of the Prophet's river to the seals of paradise's wine.
